newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down by 16 to 812 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down by 16 to 812 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 812 as of August 30, down 16 from the prior week and 41 above the year-ago total of 772, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by 19 to 681, while rigs working offshore rose by five to 111. The number of rigs active in inland waters dipped by two to 20.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed a decrease of 17 and Wyoming, which rose by five. Michigan dropped by three.

A total of 288 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down nine from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas dipped by six to 493, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects edged down one to 31.
There were 173 rigs drilling directionally, 66 drilling horizontally and 573 drilling vertically.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by one to 293 versus 222 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
